title_zh: 面向未见组合故障的异构多无人机零样本协同恢复：动作条件故障交互分解
title_en: Action-Conditioned Fault-Interaction Decomposition for Zero-Shot Cooperative Recovery under Unseen Compound Failures in Heterogeneous Multi-UAV Teams
core_question: Can action-conditioned low-order fault interactions learned from nominal, single-fault, and selected pair-fault cases support zero-shot recovery decisions for held-out compound failures?
single_core_innovation: factor recovery-action value by primitive-fault main effects and action-conditioned fault interactions, then use a preregistered task-dependency graph to regularize—not define—the interaction support

fault_observability.decision_input: causally available degraded subsystem indicators and local mission state
forbidden: held-out combination identity as a categorical training label
fault_observability.claim_boundary: the study addresses recovery from previously unseen combinations of detected primitive degradation signatures, not zero-shot fault diagnosis

train_test_contract.training_support: nominal + all single faults + preregistered subset of pair faults
train_test_contract.zero_shot_test: disjoint held-out pairs, triples, and quadruples
train_test_contract.no_leakage: held-out combinations cannot appear in training, curriculum, model selection, normalization fitting, or hyperparameter selection
train_test_contract.selection_split: a separate validation subset of seen combinations is used for model selection

p0_gates.G1_learnability: nominal and single-fault oracle policies are learnable; fault cases are neither ceiling-saturated nor globally collapsed
p0_gates.G2_nonadditivity: at least three preregistered pair faults show interaction magnitude larger than uncertainty/noise and practically relevant to return or success
p0_gates.G3_decision_relevance: at least three pair faults change the optimal recovery-action ranking relative to the additive prediction
p0_gates.G4_additive_insufficiency: an additive fault model has materially worse held-out action-regret or value prediction than a second-order model
p0_gates.G5_low_order_generalization: the second-order model improves held-out-combination action-regret on a disjoint P0 test split without using RL training
p0_gates.G6_structural_alignment: interaction magnitude or predictive utility is associated with preregistered task-dependency proximity under a permutation/null test

p0_measurement.uncertainty: state-blocked bootstrap; cloned action evaluations are not treated as independent training seeds

pilot_after_p0_only.budget: 3 seeds x 1M environment steps per method
pilot_after_p0_only.authorization_rule: all G1-G6 must pass before any learning pilot starts

theory_claims.safe_now: a uniform action-value approximation error epsilon implies greedy-action regret at most 2 epsilon
theory_claims.research_target: derive structural interaction sparsity or decay under explicit conditional-independence and finite-horizon assumptions
theory_claims.forbidden_until_proved: claiming graph-distance decay, sample-complexity improvement, or exact zero interactions

stop_rules: stop if G2 or G3 fails: the environment lacks decision-relevant fault interaction
stop if G5 fails: second-order compositionality is not supported
stop if G6 fails: remove the topology-structure claim and do not proceed as the proposed main topic
do not tune gates after observing failures
do not launch the 9M pilot before a signed P0 report
